## Why a bespoke format might be cleaner

The current maths book inherits the Quarto book shell, then replaces parts of
it with Wayward website chrome, then patches the remaining seams with CSS and
JavaScript. That makes every layout decision harder than it needs to be.

### Where the collisions happen

- book sidebar versus injected site header
- native Quarto content grid versus custom full-width reading layouts
- native repo tools versus rewritten links
- page footer expectations versus after-body injection

### What a dedicated format would own

1. Typography and spacing
2. Sidebar look and collapse behavior
3. TOC placement and width
4. Footer content and presentation
5. Theme tokens and book-only utilities

::: {.callout-note}
This page is deliberately plain in content so we can judge the shell rather
than the prose.
:::

## A simple section for testing

The native Quarto book structure is already doing most of the right things. The
main question is whether we can make it feel like Wayward House without trying
to turn it into the main site itself.

### Another section

This mock should give us a cleaner basis for deciding whether to build a full
custom template, or whether a custom format plus native Quarto book components
is already enough.
